parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both controllers are Express HTTP adapters, which is a cohesive concern. However, TaskController copies the Task-to-response mapping four times, including the rule that dueDate becomes an ISO string or null. That rule should live in one place. The two controllers also shape responses differently: ProjectController sends the raw entity from the use case, while TaskController maps each entity to an explicit response object. The error-to-400 handling is also copied in all five handlers across both files. This is duplication of a serialization rule plus an inconsistent response abstraction, so the unit fails the rubric.

violations.message: The Task response format (field list and the dueDate ISO/null rule) is copied by hand in createTask, assignTask, markTaskAsDone and listTasks instead of living in one shared mapper.

createProject sends the raw use-case result (res.status(201).json(project)), while TaskController maps entities to explicit response objects. The error-to-400 handling is also copied rather than shared across the controllers.
